finding.description: A library with published vulnerabilities is loaded on every page.

recommendation.goal: What is the recommended fix for this web security flaw: outdated-library (A library with published vulnerabilities is loaded on every page. Evidence: jQuery v1.8.3 banner). State the concrete fix and cite a primary source (OWASP, MDN, NIST, PCI DSS, IETF RFC, or the vendor's own advisory).
recommendation.answer: Recommended fix: Update the version of the dependency in the project on a testing environment. If all tests succeed, the update can be pushed to production. This addresses jQuery v1.8.3 loaded on every page by updating to a non-vulnerable version. No specific patched jQuery version number is stated on the cited OWASP page; inventory/remove-unused steps omitted for lack of primary-source wording. Confidence 8/10 means high confidence in OWASP wording, not in version number.

fix.summary: Remove the vulnerable jQuery 1.8.3 endpoint by redirecting it to the catalogue.
fix.risk: Any client-side code expecting jQuery at that URL will no longer receive JavaScript.

applied.find: if (path === '/js/jquery-1.8.3.min.js') return [200, { 'content-type': 'application/javascript' }, '/*! jQuery v1.8.3 jquery.com | jquery.org/license */ window.jQuery=window.$=function(){};']; // FLAW 14: outdated library (CVE-2020-11022, CVE-2020-11023)
applied.replace: if (path === '/js/jquery-1.8.3.min.js') return [302, { location: '/' }, '']; // removed vulnerable jQuery 1.8.3
